evidence: Ov. Ars 2.10: longē quem petō portus abest
Cic. Quinct. 79: quam longē est hinc in saltum Gallicānum? (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: With esse and abesse: longē abest, it’s far; nōn longē, not far; longē ā (ab), far from; further is longius (longius nōn discēdam, I won’t go any further: Cic. Fam. 14.2, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: far off, in the distance, from afar
evidence: Cic. Cat. 2.29: nōn jam procul, sed hīc praesentēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of what is seen, heard, or kept far away: procul hinc, keep away! (Mart. 13.25.1).

evidence: Cic. Imp. Pomp. 47: ex locīs tam longinquīs (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: quid properās, juvenis? mediīs tua pīnus in undīs nāvigat, et longē quem petō portus abest
phrases.english: why the hurry, young man? your ship is out in mid-sea, and the harbour I’m making for is far away
Far be it from me to say.
to be a long way off
to be a long way off

phrases.latin: Longēne abest? — Nōn longē; mox aderimus.
phrases.english: Is it far? — Not far; we’ll soon be there.
It isn’t far from the stadium.

phrases.latin: ā quō locō fundus is dē quō agitur nōn longē abest
phrases.english: not far from which lies the farm this case is about
Can you see the ship in the distance, out at sea?

phrases.latin: et jam summa procul vīllārum culmina fūmant
phrases.english: and already the rooftops of the farmhouses are smoking in the distance

phrases.latin: sed Ergasilus estne hic, procul quem videō?
phrases.english: but is that Ergasilus I see there in the distance?
It’s far; we’ll take the bus.

phrases.latin: Tam longē est mihi quam Terentiānus, quī nunc Nīliacam regit Syēnēn.
phrases.english: He is as far away from me as Terentianus, who now governs Syene on the Nile.

sources: Lewis & Short: longe · Lewis & Short: procul · Lewis & Short: longinquus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 173, 313.
